correctness.rationale: The precise \(d\ge4\) local claim follows from the squared Euclidean barycentric formula, strict diameter localization to d(d+1) ordered vertex pairs, the weighted tangent-cone Jacobian 1/4, and exact radial root r−Q(theta)r²=s. Uniform boundedness of Q makes Lagrange inversion and integration exchange valid, producing an all-order convergent series. A Dirichlet moment identity yields all coefficients as rational numbers. The exact norms 4d−3 and 2d² give the leading constant and first correction 3(d−1)/(2d+1). In d=4, rational fourth moments yield E Q²=533/5280 and second correction 34/15. The extracted standalone Python checker independently verifies polynomial moments, Catalan–Lagrange coefficients and seeded cone quadrature. Sampling is not the analytic proof; no global threshold or uniform-in-d conclusion is asserted.

originality.rationale: Full relevant primary texts or available material were compared with the specific Euclidean norm, regular-simplex dimension \(d\ge4\), and high-distance two-point probability. The 2026 motivating source proves general Brunn–Minkowski and small-distance relations, not the endpoint coefficients. Existing exact tetrahedron and equilateral-triangle formulas motivate exclusion of \(d\le3\). The closest published same-simplex beta theorem measures the Minkowski gauge of the difference body, and is mathematically non-equivalent to Euclidean distance: equal-gauge vectors can have distinct lengths. General chord-to-distance relations do not supply the missing higher-dimensional chord function. Unindexed historical results remain possible.
residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be proved by negative search results; older higher-dimensional simplex autocorrelation or radial-covariogram work may exist under other names.
The 2021 general chord-to-distance article and the 2012 planar triangle full texts were not inspected in full; only claims actually accessible were compared.
The exact convergence radius in dimension d and any uniform-in-d behavior are not determined.

value.rationale: The invariant is the natural rare near-diametral two-point distance tail for volume-uniform regular simplices. Beyond correctness or a small arbitrary slice, the result resolves the full endpoint analytic germ in every previously untreated higher dimension, with explicit rational moments and a positive series in the squared deficit. It identifies exponent 2d, sharp dimension-dependent leading and first correction constants, and a new dimension-four second correction. These quantities benchmark higher-dimensional covariogram calculations and characterize the scarcity of almost diametral chords. It claims no universal theorem for arbitrary bodies and no inflated independent validation.
